_about: Anatomically Programmed Radiography (APR) chart. Selecting a protocol sets technique (kVp/mAs), anti-scatter grid, display LUT, SID, collimated field, and receptor size/orientation for that projection. Grouped body part -> region -> projection. Typical adult DR values: distal extremities 50-65 kVp no grid at 100 cm SID; proximal limb/skull/spine/abdomen/pelvis 70-90 kVp with grid at 100 cm; chest high-kVp 110-125 kVp with grid at 180 cm. coll = collimated field [width_cm, length_cm]; det = receptor [short_cm, long_cm]; orient = portrait/landscape. Teaching approximations, not a facility chart. cm = the adult thickness (caliper, along the central ray) an entry is written for: the console measures the patient there and scales mAs at fixed kV (src/core/technique.js). Entries without it are used as written. mAs calibrated on this simulator (Oct 2026): each exam exposed at its chart technique on the shipped subjects, read with the exam VOI, and its mAs moved to the station that brings DI to 0 (size-corrected exams are calibrated for the chart thickness). Lateral cervical and lateral forearm/elbow are not: their central rays cross anatomy that is not the exam's (the head and neck CT has the arms raised beside the head; the arm lies against the trunk). AP cervical is centred on C4 from the CT's own vertebra labels and read by caliper like the trunk. aec = the ionisation chambers the exam meters on (l/c/r), standard positioning practice: the two lateral chambers over the lungs for a PA chest, all three for abdomen and pelvis, the centre for spine, skull and the gridded limbs. A protocol selects them; whether AEC is used stays the operator's choice.
_reference: Merrill's Atlas / Bontrager positioning references for SID, receptor size, and collimation; grid + kVp per body-part attenuation.

_pose: pose.roll: degrees about the long axis from the subject's rest pose (body subjects rest supine/AP; the hand rests PA); +roll lifts world +x. pose.cc: central-ray angle, negative = cephalic. pose.centre: a landmark in landmarks.json (measured by tools/measure_landmarks.py) that the patient is moved to put under the central ray. pose.through: an angled central ray is aimed through that point, as a radiographer aims it, the patient moved along the table by the point's height above the receptor times the angle's tangent; without it the point is placed over the receptor's centre. pose.fidelity "approx" marks a view a rigid model cannot truly achieve; pose.note says why.
_paste: paste: a long-length study stitched from several images (src/pasting.js, src/core/pasting.js), taken at the wall stand or the table with the tube tilted about its focal spot over a tracking bucky. paste.coi: the default centre of interest, cm of the anatomy above the cover or tabletop (the plane the stitched image's ruler is calibrated at); paste.limits: the landmarks the superior and inferior limits are set just beyond. mAs is written for 180 cm and follows the room's pasting distance by the inverse square.
